interest: This file provides valuable insight into the commercial and administrative complexities of Japan's economic rehabilitation during the early Allied occupation. It highlights the direct friction between SCAP's tightly managed foreign trade controls—specifically the requirement that Japanese exports be sold f.o.b. with insurance and freight placed abroad—and the interests of private American corporations like the American Foreign Insurance Association seeking to resume commercial operations in Japan. The exchange also documents inter-agency administrative mechanisms among the Far Eastern Commission, the Department of State's Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs, and the Department of the Army's Civil Affairs Division, while the accompanying charge-out slips illustrate how these records were referenced in State Department administrative workflows throughout the 1950s.
overview: This file comprises records concerning marine insurance underwriting for Japanese exports during the Allied occupation of Japan following World War II. The central issue is an inquiry by the American Foreign Insurance Association (AFIA) to the Far Eastern Commission regarding instructions from the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) requiring Japanese export sales to be contracted f.o.b. with freight and insurance paid by the consignee, a condition AFIA argued effectively barred its newly licensed Tokyo branch from placing marine coverage in Japan. The file contains AFIA's letter of November 14, 1947, the State Department's reply of November 25, 1947 clarifying SCAP's trade policies and facilitating discussions with the Army's Civil Affairs Division, and eight subsequent Department of State charge-out slips dating from 1956 to 1958 tracking file loans related to this and associated decimal files.

subfiles.about: The American Foreign Insurance Association requests clarification from the Far Eastern Commission regarding SCAP instructions that consignees pay export freight and insurance, which impedes AFIA's marine underwriting in Japan.
subfiles.from: L. H. Doman, General Counsel, American Foreign Insurance Association
subfiles.summary: L. H. Doman, General Counsel of the American Foreign Insurance Association (AFIA), writes to the Far Eastern Commission regarding the recent licensing of AFIA representative Warren W. Provost by SCAP on October 20, 1947. Doman expresses concern over reported SCAP directives stipulating that export letters of credit require insurance and freight to be paid by consignees, which effectively mandates placing insurance abroad rather than in Japan. He explains that reviving marine insurance was a primary reason for reopening their Japanese branch, and argues that American insurance activities align with U.S. policy to revive peaceful Japanese economic activity. He requests verification of SCAP's orders and asks for an opportunity to confer on the matter in Washington.
subfiles.title: Letter from L. H. Doman (AFIA) to Frank A. Turner (Far Eastern Commission) regarding SCAP Marine Insurance Regulations
subfiles.to: Frank A. Turner, Research and Analysis Secretary, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: The Department of State explains SCAP's policy on f.o.b. export terms and coordinates a consultation between AFIA and the Department of the Army's Civil Affairs Division.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Acting Chief, Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs, Department of State
keywords: Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: Roswell H. Whitman responds on behalf of the Department of State to L. H. Doman's inquiry referred by the Far Eastern Commission concerning SCAP insurance rules. Whitman states that while SCAP intends Japanese export sales to be contracted f.o.b. Japanese ports, it is doubtful this policy was intended to bar Japanese buyers from securing insurance coverage from American firms established in Japan. He notes that he discussed the matter with Lieutenant Colonel Nagle of the Army's Civil Affairs Division in Washington, D.C. Whitman concludes by inviting Doman to meet with Colonel Nagle on his next visit to Washington.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman (Department of State) to L. H. Doman (AFIA) regarding Japanese Export Sales and Insurance Coverage
subfiles.to: L. H. Doman, General Counsel, American Foreign Insurance Association
